frame.origin: centre of the segmentation volume's bounding box
frame.axes: the dataset's own axes: x and y lie in the section plane, z is the sectioning axis
frame.layerAxisFrom: 782 reconstructed cells with a layer call, seunglabdata assets/mec/cells/cells.json

basisNote: columns: the dataset x, y, z axes in atlas (page) coordinates, chosen so the measured pia direction (layer VI to layer I) equals the outward normal of the brain surface nearest the placed centre, read from the page's own atlas meshes, and the sectioning axis is as close to dorsoventral as that allows (horizontal sections)
centreNote: offset from the page's left ENTm centroid: nudged 0.7 mm dorsal on the builders' advice (they went for as dorsal a piece of MEC as they could get), then pulled inward so the block's pia face lies on the atlas brain surface

population.note: Cell types are PRESUMED: called from nucleus size, then checked against the cell's layer. The number of neurons is not known. At least 14,112 nuclei carry a neuron type name; the rest sit in unnamed clusters mixing interneurons with glia and vasculature.
population.src: nucleus annotations carrying layer and nucleus-size cluster, read 2026-09-22

synapseNote: No synapse table: the volume's CAVE annotation and materialization services were still being provisioned when this was built (annotation 404, materialize 503), so the cells are drawn without synapses.
placement: Drawn in the left atlas ENTm at the block's true size, a little dorsal of the region's centroid with its pia face on the brain surface, turned so the block's measured layer axis follows the surface and its sections lie horizontal. The EM block is NOT registered to the atlas; the hemisphere was not recorded, and the dorsal nudge and the horizontal cut come from the builders' description, not a measurement.

mesh.source: connectome.quest/mec gallery web tier (seunglabdata assets/mec/gallery), built from the pni_mec meshing service, nuclei resolved to the live chunkedgraph on 2026-09-29
mesh.glb: float32 positions, trimesh export; the page computes normals

cellsNote: Seven cells, one per type the connectome.quest gallery shows. Four were named by eye by Amy Sterling and matched to the live segmentation; three are automatic calls from nucleus size, marked predicted. Glia subtypes from nucleus size are unreliable in this volume (two of them were swapped on inspection), which is why the predicted ones say so.

provenance.built_by: Eric Hammerschmith with Zhihao Zheng, Seung Lab, Princeton
